\subsection{Replicate variance on the ablation grid}
\label{sec:tier-noise}

We ran the leave-one-out ablation over four model tiers on
\textsc{subset20b}, a 20-task split of LakeQA stratified jointly on node
count and historical solve rate. Every axis is held at the oracle and one
axis is degraded per cell, giving seven cells per model. Each cell was run
\textbf{three times} under identical configuration, so every number carries
a standard deviation rather than resting on a single sample.

That replication is the central result. The mean per-cell standard
deviation is 6.4\,pp, so a two-sigma interval spans
$\pm13$\,pp and an effect must exceed roughly 13\,pp to be
distinguishable from run-to-run variance. Since one task is worth 5\,pp at
$n=20$, that threshold is about 3 tasks.

Of the 24 degraded cells, only
5 clear that threshold: Search: BM25 at \texttt{gpt-5.4-nano} ($-25.0$\,pp), Plan: Default at \texttt{gpt-5.2} ($-20.0$\,pp), Search: BM25 at \texttt{gpt-5-mini} ($-16.7$\,pp), Search: BM25 at \texttt{gpt-5.2} ($-15.0$\,pp), Search: PNEUMA at \texttt{gpt-5-mini} ($-15.0$\,pp).
4 of those are search degradations, on 3 of the
4 tiers; the remaining cells cannot be separated from noise
at this sample size. Search costs the most accuracy of any axis, but it
clears the threshold on the weaker tiers and not on the strongest --
the same degradation hurts less as the model improves.

The reference cells themselves are \texttt{gpt-5.4-nano} 41.7\% ($\sigma=2.9$), \texttt{gpt-5-mini} 73.3\% ($\sigma=2.9$), \texttt{gpt-5.2} 71.7\% ($\sigma=10.4$), \texttt{gpt-5.6-luna} 75.0\% ($\sigma=5.0$).
The two strongest, \texttt{gpt-5.6-luna} and \texttt{gpt-5-mini}, differ by
1.7\,pp against a standard error of 3.3\,pp on that
difference, so they are not separable here.

Accuracy is not what separates the tiers. Over all cells the top three
land within 7.9\,pp of one another
(64.0--71.9\%), inside the replicate threshold,
while cost per correct answer spans
13$\times$:
\texttt{gpt-5.6-luna} answers at \$0.0207 in
10.1 agent cycles against \texttt{gpt-5.2} at
\$0.2760 in 16.3. The tier that
costs the most buys nothing here that the cheapest does not already
provide.
